areas_of_law: Contract law - enforceability of termination clause
Human rights - disability discrimination/duty to accommodate
issues: Whether the termination clause limiting notice to ESA minimums is enforceable, given it purports to allow termination for cause on a lower threshold than the ESA's wilful misconduct standard
Whether the 2019 contract amendment is void for lack of fresh consideration
What length of reasonable notice at common law Dana is entitled to given her age, length of service, position, and availability of comparable employment (Bardal factors)
Whether Dana was terminated shortly after returning from medical leave/graduated return to work constitutes discrimination or failure to accommodate a disability under the Human Rights Code
Whether requiring execution of a full and final release within 5 days as a condition of receiving benefits/ESA-mandated payments is enforceable or violates the ESA
Whether Dana is entitled to benefits continuation and bonus for the reasonable notice period
What limitation periods and statutory deadlines apply to Dana's wrongful dismissal, human rights, and ESA claims
key_facts: Dana Reyes, 54 years old, employed as Operations Manager from March 2012 to August 14, 2026 (~14 years, 5 months)
Salary $98,000/year plus benefits and 10% annual bonus
Employer Northline Logistics Inc., ~180 employees, Ontario payroll well above $3 million (relevant to ESA severance entitlement)
In 2019, presented with new contract under threat of exclusion from restructuring; no new consideration given
Termination clause limits notice to ESA minimums and allows termination for cause for 'any breach of Company policy' without notice
Contract silent on post-termination benefits continuation
Dana took medical leave Feb-June 2026 after spinal surgery; doctor recommended graduated return (4-hour days for 6 weeks)
Manager emailed stating need for someone who can commit to full days shortly before return
Dana terminated without cause three weeks after returning to work
Termination letter offered only 8 weeks' pay in lieu of notice
Benefits and further payments conditioned on signing a full and final release within 5 days
Dana has not signed the release
Dana applied to ~30 comparable jobs with no offers, relevant to mitigation and reasonable notice
causes_of_action: Discrimination on basis of disability under the Ontario Human Rights Code (failure to accommodate, adverse treatment linked to medical leave/return to work)
Claim for ESA minimum standards violations (notice, severance, benefits continuation)
Potential bad faith in manner of dismissal / breach of duty of good faith and fair dealing
candidate_statutes: Employment Standards Act, 2000 - O. Reg. 288/01 (severance/termination regulations)
